explanation: Command-line arguments in C are parameters passed to a program when it is executed from the command line. They allow the program to receive external input, such as options or file names, making the program more flexible and interactive. This concept is used to handle user-specified data without hardcoding values, enabling dynamic behavior based on runtime inputs.
